steps.do: Create the candidate prompt the Evaluations will score. Click Prompts (under Prompt lifecycle), click New prompt, choose Write / paste, paste the text below into Prompt text, give it a Prompt name and click Create and Open.
fill: You answer support tickets and incident alerts using ONLY the evidence you are given. State what the evidence says and nothing more; if it does not cover the question, say so and escalate to a person.
steps.see: The prompt opens on its workspace with a Versions panel showing version 1.

steps.do: Load the 50-row test set. With the prompt open, click the Calibration tab. Under Eval Dataset, use Upload JSON/JSONL to choose aggregated-outputs.jsonl, type a Dataset name and click Upload Dataset. Each line becomes one example: input is the ticket or alert, expected is the evidence the answer must stay within, tags say what the row is for.
steps.see: A green line reads Uploaded 50 examples to judge-certification-set. Under Test Sets the set is listed at version 51 (one version per appended example).

steps.do: Define the judge. Open Judges (under Agent resources) and click + New Judge. Set Name and Returns bool, and paste the Instructions from faithfulness-judge.judge.json. Try a bad template first: instructions Is {{ outputs }} faithful to {{ evidence }}? are refused. The instructions may use only {{ inputs }}, {{ outputs }}, {{ expectations }}, {{ conversation }} and {{ trace }}.
steps.see: The bad template shows request body validation failed: instructions use unsupported template variable(s) {{ evidence }}; only … are allowed in red and nothing is saved. The real instructions create an active FaithfulnessJudge in the Judges list.

steps.do: Add a deliberately weak judge to prove the check can say no. Click + New Judge again: name it LenientJudge, Returns bool, instructions Return true when {{ outputs }} is a complete, well-formed answer to {{ inputs }}. Return false only if it is empty or cut off.
fill: Return true when {{ outputs }} is a complete, well-formed answer to {{ inputs }}. Return false only if it is empty or cut off.

steps.do: Score the baseline. Open Evaluations, click Run evaluation, pick Test set judge-certification-set (v51), label it baseline, leave What to score on Model completion (generic). Under Graders untick Exact match and Token F1, keep Contains expected, tick Non-empty, and under Custom LLM judges tick FaithfulnessJudge. Click Run. (This needs a model behind the server: on the simulated default it fails closed with evaluation requires a real LLM provider.)
steps.see: A baseline row appears with status completed and 50/50 examples passed.

steps.do: Score the candidate the same way. Click Run evaluation again, same test set and graders, label candidate, set What to score to Prompt version and Prompt (name@version) to grounded-reply@1. Click Run.

Read the per-example results. Open the candidate run: one row per example with the input, the expected evidence, the prediction and a score per grader. Use Compare to to pick the baseline run: the cards and rows now show the change against it. Note that the baseline's judge score is high only because a vague reply makes no claim to contradict; the deterministic Contains expected grader is what shows it said nothing useful. That is why one aggregate hides disagreement.
steps.see: With the lab's stand-in model: overall 74% for the candidate, Contains expected 66%, FaithfulnessJudge 56%, against the baseline's 67% overall (Contains expected 0%, FaithfulnessJudge 100%). A real model gives different numbers.

steps.do: Create the human-review queue. Open Review Queues (under Operate), click New queue, name it faithfulness-certification. Question 1: key faithful, type pass_fail, title the faithfulness question from review-questions.json. Click + Add question: key evidence, type text, title Evidence you checked the output against. Click Create queue.
steps.see: The queue appears in the list with 2 questions and no items.

steps.do: Enqueue ten traces and answer them. First write the 50 recorded outputs as traces with seed_traces.py (it prints a row-to-trace-id map). Open the queue, paste the ids of J01, J02, J03, J04, J05, J08, J09, J11, J14 and J26 into Add traces to review and click Enqueue. For each item click Pass or Fail as the human_label in the dataset file says, paste that row's expected JSON into the evidence box, and click Submit review. Keep the evidence box to the evidence: whatever you put there becomes {{ expectations }} for the judge in the next step.
steps.see: Items (10) in the list; each flips to completed as you submit, ending on All items reviewed. The answers are written back to each trace.

steps.where: Agent resources › Judges › FaithfulnessJudge › Try it › Human alignment
steps.do: Check the judge against the people. In Judges click Try it on FaithfulnessJudge and switch to Human alignment. Choose faithfulness-certification in the Import from Review Queue… list, pick its pass/fail question, click Import labels, then Check alignment.
steps.see: Imported 10 completed label(s); skipped 0. Then, with the stand-in model: Agreement 80%, Cohen's κ 0.60, over 10/10 examples, FP 1 · FN 1. If the judge cannot run the panel adds 10 example(s) could not be judged and are left out of the numbers with the reason. Ten rows meet the numbers but not the lab's 30-row minimum: a readout, not a certification (the API run over all 50 certifies at 0.82 / 0.6365).

steps.where: Agent resources › Judges › LenientJudge › Try it › Human alignment
steps.do: Run the same check on the weak judge: Try it on LenientJudge, Human alignment, import the same queue and question, Check alignment.
steps.see: With the stand-in model: Agreement 60%, Cohen's κ 0.20, FP 4 · FN 0. It never fails a wrong answer, so it is rejected.

steps.do: Close the loop on every disagreement. Open Test Sets, open judge-certification-set, click + Add example, paste the row's input and expected JSON, tag it judge-disagreement and click Save. Do it for J03 (the judge passed what a person failed) and J14 (the judge failed what a person passed). Then reword the judge's instructions or the review question so they say the same thing, rerun Evaluations and the alignment check, and do not certify until it clears. (Capture from trace would store the trace's own reply as the expected answer, which is the wrong evidence here.)
steps.see: The set shows 52 active examples at version 53, and the two hard cases are in every later run.
steps.asset: Test set grown with the disagreements
